links.outcome: Calibration of self-reported confidence versus observed accuracy across six LLMs
links.effect: Mean self-reported confidence exceeded observed accuracy in all models; Gemini-Flash-3 had the best confidence-based discrimination and ChatGPT-5.4 the lowest expected calibration error.
links.quote: Confidence reliability also varied across models: Gemini-Flash-3 showed the highest confidence-based discrimination, ChatGPT-5.4 had the lowest expected calibration error, and mean self-reported confidence exceeded observed accuracy in all models.

links.outcome: LLM accuracy in locally specific regulatory domains versus Statistics and Epidemiology
links.effect: Performance was significantly lower in Israeli-specific domains (MoH Directives, Reports and Committees, Legislation and Regulations) than in Statistics and Epidemiology; top model accuracy was 77.9% overall.
links.quote: More importantly, performance was significantly lower in domains requiring locally specific knowledge, including Israeli Ministry of Health Directives, Reports and Committees, and Legislation and Regulations, compared with Statistics and Epidemiology.

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance and confidence calibration on medical administration board exam questions.
